 Regina Kim, Contributor Updated Tue, 10 November 2026 at 9:50 pm UTC 7 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. BOYNEXTDOOR perform onstage at Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden on November 7.
 Courtesy of KOZ Entertainment (HYBE) After a string of sold-out concerts across Korea and Japan, K-pop boy band BOYNEXTDOOR have brought their first world tour, KNOCK ON Vol. 2 , to North America. The tour's 10-city North American leg kicked off in Dallas on October 30 and most recently stopped in New York City, where the group's six members Sungho, Riwoo, Jaehyun, Taesan, Leehan and Woonhak performed for thousands of fans at Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden on November 7.
 The tour follows sold-out shows in Seoul, Busan, Osaka, Chiba and Nagano earlier this year, with upcoming performances in Taiwan and Hong Kong in 2027 having already sold out as well.
 BOYNEXTDOOR debuted in 2023 under KOZ ENTERTAINMENT, a HYBE subsidiary founded by Korean rapper and producer Zico. In an already crowded K-pop landscape, the sextet quickly set themselves apart by co-writing and co-producing many of their songs . Like their name that reflects their approachable "boy next door" image, the group focuses on creating music that feels authentic, relatable and rooted in everyday experiences.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Within just a few years, six of their albums have entered the Billboard 200—four of which have sold over a million copies each—and the group has performed at Lollapalooza Chicago. In recent months BOYNEXTDOOR released HOME: DELUXE , a repackaged edition of their first studio album HOME , and launched their own video podcast series DAMN!BULANCE on STAN:A, HYBE Media Studio's original video podcast channel.
 Now the group is building on their growing momentum with their first North American tour. For fans planning to attend one of BOYNEXTDOOR's upcoming North American shows, here are six things to expect, based on their November 7 th concert in NYC.
 'The Ordinary Jackpot' Star Lee Jun-Hyuk On Acting And What Drives Him 
 1. The setlist highlights BOYNEXTDOOR's stylistic range, spanning different genres and featuring both their biggest hits and lesser-known tracks.
 The setlist offers a wide selection of the group's varied repertoire, from their popular hits like "Earth, Wind & Fire," "Hollywood Action" and "IF I SAY, I LOVE YOU" to B-sides like "123-78," "Forever You" and "So let's go see the stars."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement According to KOZ ENTERTAINMENT, BOYNEXTDOOR's North American setlist was designed to showcase their musical versatility while appealing to the tastes of local audiences. Clocking in at approximately 2.5 hours, the show also features several encore tracks, including repeat performances of the pop-rock anthem "ADIOS!" and the high-octane EDM banger "ANIMAL" (the lead single from the group's latest album, HOME: DELUXE ), which momentarily transformed the concert into a rave .
 Bright, colorful lights and dynamic visuals further enhance the group's performances, often casting the members in striking silhouettes—though some of the strobe effects might prove a bit too intense for concertgoers sensitive to flashing lights.
 BOYNEXTDOOR at the Theater at MSG in NYC
 2. English subtitles are displayed onscreen during select BOYNEXTDOOR songs to help fans better appreciate the lyrics.
 For a couple of songs—namely the fan song "I Wonder" and the poignant "Forever You"—English subtitles are shown onscreen to help the audience better understand the meaning behind the Korean lyrics.
 "Even though we speak different languages, we hope you can feel the emotion in the melody. So let every lyric speak to your heart," Taesan told the crowd while introducing "Forever You," a song the group wrote while "thinking about our families and the people we love."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As all six members sat on stools onstage and took turns singing the verses, English subtitles appeared in the background (though the small, semi-cursive font might have made the lyrics difficult to read for some concertgoers ).
 3. One of the show's intermissions turns into a karaoke session, with fans invited to sing along to BOYNEXTDOOR songs.
 While the English subtitles helped convey the meaning behind certain songs, it seemed that much of the audience already knew many of the lyrics by heart.
 During one of the intermissions, the music videos for "Earth, Wind & Fire" and "Hollywood Action"—two of the group's biggest hits—played on massive screens as the crowd enthusiastically sang along in both Korean and English without missing a beat.
 It was an impressive feat, especially considering how fast some of the Korean verses are sung and how quickly the romanized lyrics flashed by onscreen. (Even this Korean speaker—who admittedly doesn't know the lyrics to either song—couldn't keep up.)

 4. Chances are you'll probably find a very diverse crowd—fans of all ages, races, ethnicities and genders—at a BOYNEXTDOOR concert.
 While this probably comes as no surprise to K-pop fans who regularly attend concerts, believe it or not, I still encounter many Americans who seem to think that most K-pop fans in the U.S. are Korean or Korean American. For most K-pop concerts in the U.S.—especially those featuring newer groups like BOYNEXTDOOR—the vast majority of the audience is not of Korean descent.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement At BOYNEXTDOOR's New York show at Infosys Theater, I saw concertgoers of all races and ethnicities—white, Black, Latino, South Asian, you name it—and fans of all ages, from tween girls to men and women who looked to be in their fifties or sixties.
 Just before the concert started, while I was looking for a water fountain, an older white woman approached me and asked me if I was a "member." Thinking she meant a Chase cardmember (since Chase cardholders can receive certain perks at Madison Square Garden-owned venues in NYC), I was about to say "yes" when she explained that members of ONEDOOR (the official name for BOYNEXTDOOR's fanbase) could pick up a free BOYNEXTDOOR photocard.
 She excitedly told me that she'd gotten one and offered to show me where I could pick up mine. (I smiled and explained that I was just looking for the water fountain.)
 5. Get ready to see the members of BOYNEXTDOOR pull off some impressive solo dance moves between performances. Oh, and a little bass guitar from Taesan, too.
 Beyond the synchronized choreography that accompanies most of their songs, BOYNEXTDOOR's members also found opportunities to showcase their individual dance skills between sets.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement At the NYC concert, the members took turns showing off moves ranging from breakdancing to shuffling to even bokko dance (a retro Korean dance that blends techno and disco, with an emphasis on exaggerated arm movements).
 And singing and dancing weren't the only talents on display: concertgoers were also treated to Taesan playing bass guitar during "Nice Guy."
 6. Expect lots of interaction between BOYNEXTDOOR and the audience. 
 BOYNEXTDOOR don't just perform for their fans—they actively encourage the audience to become part of the show.
 Throughout the concert, the members made a concerted effort to connect with their fans, frequently addressing them in English despite the language barrier and encouraging them to participate in various ways. They invited the crowd to sing along, jump, turn on their phone flashlights and, at one point, even do the wave.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement These playful exchanges clearly illustrated just how much the members enjoy engaging with their fans, making the show feel more fun and personal even in a theater packed with thousands of strangers.
 Fans holding lightsticks at BOYNEXTDOOR's concert in NYC
 Below are the dates for the North American leg of BOYNEXTDOOR's KNOCK ON Vol. 2 tour:

 Sat, Nov 7 – New York, NY – Infosys Theater at MSG
 Tues, Nov 10 – Toronto, ON – Queen Elizabeth Theatre
 Fri, Nov 13 – Vancouver, BC – Queen Elizabeth Theatre
 Sun, Nov 15 – Seattle, WA – Showbox SoDo
 Tues, Nov 17 – San Francisco, CA – The Warfield
 Fri, Nov 20 – Los Angeles, CA – Peacock Theater
